steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Both Kodály and Bartók collected and transcribed Hungarian folk songs — their art music transforms folk material through modernist techniques. | Key Fact: Bartók's polymodality combines multiple modes simultaneously, creating harmonic complexity while maintaining folk-like melodic identity. | Key Fact: Irregular metre (5/8, 7/8) reflects Hungarian folk rhythm — the distinctive short-long pattern creates a characteristic uneven groove. | Key Fact: String techniques expand traditional sound: pizzicato (plucked), col legno (wood of bow), sul ponticello (near bridge for glassy tone).
